posts.title: A handbook before the funding round
posts.excerpt: A 60-person software company in Cork had its handbook and contracts rebuilt in 5 weeks, before a funding round.
posts.content:
The situation

A software company in Cork employed 60 people. It asked Ito HR Partners to rebuild its employee handbook and its contracts. A funding round was the reason for the timetable. The work was finished in 5 weeks. The company is anonymised. This account does not name it, does not name any investor, and does not say what happened to the round.

The company sits in the range we work with, 15 to 400 people. The law in question was Irish employment law. Cork is in Ireland, so the file did not need a partner firm in another jurisdiction. Had the question been the law of another country, we would have stopped and referred it on, without naming that firm. That was not this file.

What we did

The matter started with a free scoping call of 30 minutes, by video. The call is €0, whether it is taken by video or at 24 Harcourt Lane, Dublin 2. On it we heard what the company needed before the round: a handbook its managers could actually use, and contracts it could issue with a straight face. We did not start drafting on the call.

Within 2 working days we sent a written fixed quote. Work of this kind is priced on the published list. An employee handbook and policies, up to 12 policies, is €2,400 fixed. A contract set, templates for 3 role types, is €980 fixed. VAT at 23% is extra on both. This account does not publish the invoice this client received, and it does not add those two fees together into a project total. The quote named the scope, and the scope was agreed in writing before drafting began.

One adviser held the file for the 5 weeks. There was a weekly check-in. The check-in was there to keep the draft inside the quote, not to open a second project. The handbook topics we write from are contracts, the handbook, leave, remote work, holiday pay, working time, payslips, statutory sick pay, grievance, disciplinary, bullying, and onboarding. Up to 12 policies is the cap. Only the policies named in the quote were written. We do not add a policy so the binder looks complete.

The contracts were templates for 3 role types. Three is the published scope of a contract set. A fourth role type would have been a new quote, not a paragraph slipped in at the end. The company was hiring into roles it already knew, and the templates were written so a manager could use them at the next start date without waiting for us to redraft from a blank page.

The drafting was in plain language. The test we use is whether a manager can follow the page without a lawyer in the room. Amara Okoye leads HR policy at the practice, and contract templates sit with Kwame Mensah's onboarding and contracts work. On a single engagement, one adviser still holds the file. We do not say which of the seven advisers was the named adviser on this anonymised matter.

The 5 weeks held the scoping call, the quote, the drafting, the weekly check-ins, and the handover. We do not break that period into a finer timetable, because the fact we were given is the 5 weeks, not a day count inside them.

Where it left them

At the end of the 5 weeks the company had a rebuilt handbook and rebuilt contracts, in writing. That written handover is what they kept. Follow-up questions on those documents were included for 30 days. During those 30 days, as on any enquiry to the practice, we reply within 1 working day. Our hours are Mon–Fri 9:00–17:30, Irish time.

We do not say the funding round closed. We do not say the new documents prevented a dispute, sped up a deal, or satisfied an investor. None of that was the engagement, and none of it is a result we claim. The investigation standard we use elsewhere, a report typically within 18 working days of the last interview, does not belong to this story. This was handbook and contract work, not a grievance.

What we can say is the work itself. The scope was agreed before we started. One adviser knew the file. The documents were written to be reused. The company left with a handbook and contracts it could put in front of its own people, rebuilt in the 5 weeks it had asked for.

A company in a similar position can start the same way. The scoping call is 30 minutes and costs nothing. Email hello@itohr.example or call +353 1 555 0142. We reply within 1 working day. If the need is wider than a handbook, the same call can point to a health check at €1,450 fixed, a payroll review at €1,900 fixed, or an investigation from €3,800. Each of those is a different quote. None of them starts until it is agreed in writing.

posts.title: Holiday pay across four sites
posts.excerpt: A 140-person hospitality group ran payroll across four sites. We reviewed one cycle, documented the holiday-pay corrections, and the group paid them.
posts.content:
The situation

A 140-person hospitality group was running payroll across four sites, each with its own way of recording working time and leave. The group wanted to know whether holiday pay was being calculated the same way everywhere.

What we did

We reviewed one payroll cycle with the group's payroll provider: holiday pay, working-time records and payslip content. The review was advisory; we did not run the payroll. We documented each correction in a written report.

Where it left them

The group paid the corrections we documented. That is the whole of what we report. A payroll compliance review is a fixed fee, agreed in writing before the work starts.

posts.title: An independent look at a grievance
posts.excerpt: A 35-person design studio asked for an independent look at a grievance. We agreed a scope, held the interviews and issued the findings report.
posts.content:
The situation

A 35-person design studio had received a grievance and wanted someone outside the team to look at it independently, so that the people involved could trust the process.

What we did

We agreed the scope of the complaint in writing first, then held the interviews and wrote a findings report. Each person was told what the process was and how the report would be used.

Where it left them

The findings report was issued 18 working days after the last interview. The timing in this matter is the timing we record, not a promise for the next one.

posts.title: What a fixed fee covers
posts.excerpt: A fixed fee is tied to a scope written down before we start. Here is what that means for a health check, a handbook and an investigation.
posts.content:
Every fee on this site is in euro and excludes VAT at 23%. The number you accept is tied to a scope written down before the work starts. A change of scope is a new written quote, not an open hourly bill.

An HR health check is €1,450 fixed: contracts, policies and payroll set-up reviewed, with a written report in 10 working days. A payroll compliance review is €1,900 fixed for one payroll cycle and up to 150 staff. An employee handbook is €2,400 fixed for up to 12 policies. An investigation starts from €3,800 for one complaint, up to six interviews and a findings report.

Retainers run at €890 a month for Essentials and €1,850 a month for Growth, with a three-month minimum and then monthly.
